Compare a separately written finite-grid reference, actual boundary-flux budgets, an upper incident-front position and a fixed near-wall region. These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved. Download and execute the supplement Run inside atlas-double-mach-2026-11-23 from the ZIP. This command executes all 1 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it. Double Mach reflection: lightweight grid verification Full 2D Euler finite volumes evolve the existing Double Mach initial/boundary data to T=.2 on64x16,128x32 and256x64 cells. Compare a separately written finite-grid reference, actual boundary-flux budgets, an upper incident-front position and a fixed near-wall region. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Nondimensional[0,4]x[0,1], gamma1.4, Mach10. Shock footx=1/6, angle60degrees; postshock(rho,u,v,p)=(8,8.25sqrt(3)/2,-4.125,116.5), upstream(1.4,0,0,1). Initial cells are classified by their centers, not exact cut-cell means. Left postshock inflow, right zero-gradient, bottom postshock forx<1/6 and slip wall otherwise; top postshock forx<1/6+(1+20t)/sqrt(3). Editorial clarification A lightweight comparison with an independent finite-grid numerical reference, not an exact2D full-field solution. Separate measured shock location, conservation budgets and wall-jet diagnostics from convergence of the thin wall jet. Forward-facing step is outside this execution scope. Adopted numerical method The published Numart piecewise-constant HLL flux, unsplit x/y divergence and Heun/SSPRK(2,2) form a small standalone package with both-stage boundary accounting and state checks. CFL.4 uses the sum of directional maximum acoustic rates; the top boundary uses each actual RK stage time. No state floor, repair or hidden retry. Before the full three-grid run, read-only review added an absent-front diagnostic guard and one test; the old contract/source are preserved and a revision contract was frozen. All21 tests, three final-time runs and40 gates passed with-W error. Previously independently executed Ny64/128 primitive MUSCL/generalized-minmod theta1.5/HLL/Heun data from the RKDG kit are reused; no reference PDE was rerun. Density L1 differences from conservatively restricted Ny128 are.08431/.05802/.03503 and pressure differences.09556/.06798/.04156. Reference64/128 increments are.00955/.01250, about.273/.301 of the finest primary differences. Maximum relative four-component boundary-budget residual is about4.60e-13. Verification limits and failures The reference is finite-grid numerical data, not an exact2D solution or an Athena/LAVA execution. The HLL family is shared, but reference spatial operators are separately written and not imported by the primary. The reference increment is an uncertainty diagnostic, not an error bound. Initial projection, sampled moving boundaries, discretization and finite-reference effects all enter the difference; the slope is no rigorous order or full reflection-pattern convergence proof. The upper-front discrepancy stays2cells while its physical width shrinks. Fixed near-wall ROIx in[1,2.75],y<=.25 is not feature tracking. Finest ROI maxu12.644 versus reference16.125 shows the thin wall jet/roll-up is unresolved. Forward step, other wall data, general perturbations, higher order and full-pattern convergence are unverified. Stored measurements and decisions Display values are rounded.
